source.version: Published IJCAI-25 proceedings paper, Special Track on Human-Centred AI (2025), printed pp. 10280-10288; identified by the proceedings footer throughout the PDF and PDF metadata. No separate revision date is stated.
source.title_on_document: Creative Momentum Transfer: How Timing and Labeling of AI Suggestions Shape Iterative Human Ideation

supplement.holds: No supplement or appendix is referred to or included in the complete PDF (pp. 1-9). No external source for unprinted arm SDs, pairwise standard errors, or model tables is identified.

paper_design_summary: An adult convenience sample, with 247 people in the stated final sample, was randomly assigned to no suggestions or to GPT-4 suggestions supplied early or late and either labeled as AI or attributed to others during two rounds of urban plastic-pollution ideation. Experts rated the resulting ideas, and semantic distance measured each submission’s alignment with the supplied AI suggestions (pp. 3-5, sections 3-4). A separate, briefly described pilot validated the stimuli, and qualitative interviews used a subset of the main sample (pp. 3-4, sections 3.2-3.4).

studies.label: Main five-condition experiment: two-round plastic-pollution ideation

assignment.what_was_assigned: Participants were assigned to Control or the four combinations of early/late GPT-4 suggestions and labeled/unlabeled attribution. Assignment was between people; scores were repeated across rounds. Web delivery is explicit, but recruitment channel and whether sessions were supervised are not stated (p. 3, sections 3.1-3.4).
assignment.quote: These participants were randomly assigned to five conditions:
assignment.prereg_locator: No preregistration statement or identifier in the PDF (pp. 1-9).

arms.name: Control
arms.description: No external suggestions in either round. Arm count is the reported final-sample count (p. 3, section 3.1); exposure description is in pp. 3-4, sections 3.3-3.4.

arms.name: Early-AI-Labeled
arms.description: GPT-4 suggestions appear in Round 1 under AI-generated ideas; no new external input in Round 2. Arm count is the reported final-sample count (p. 3, section 3.1); exposure description is in pp. 3-4, sections 3.3-3.4.

arms.name: Early-AI-Unlabeled
arms.description: The same GPT-4 suggestions appear in Round 1 under Ideas from others; no new external input in Round 2. Arm count is the reported final-sample count (p. 3, section 3.1); exposure description is in pp. 3-4, sections 3.3-3.4.

arms.name: Late-AI-Labeled
arms.description: No suggestions in Round 1; GPT-4 suggestions appear at the start of Round 2 under AI-generated ideas. Arm count is the reported final-sample count (p. 3, section 3.1); exposure description is in pp. 3-4, sections 3.3-3.4.

arms.name: Late-AI-Unlabeled
arms.description: No suggestions in Round 1; the same GPT-4 suggestions appear at the start of Round 2 under Ideas from others. Arm count is the reported final-sample count (p. 3, section 3.1); exposure description is in pp. 3-4, sections 3.3-3.4.

participants.exclusions: 254 adults initially enrolled; seven removed for failed attention checks or cursory responses, leaving the stated final sample of 247 (p. 3, section 3.1). Section 3.6 also describes removal of outliers greater than three standard deviations from the mean and incomplete responses, without counts or clarification whether these were part of the same seven exclusions (p. 4). The timing of exclusions relative to assignment and the pre-exclusion randomized total are not separately documented; n_randomized is left null. The 247 final-sample total and listed arm sizes are retained as analyzed, without inferring another count from the ANOVA degrees of freedom.
participants.who: Adult convenience sample with demographic screening for diversity in age, gender, and education. Recruitment source, occupational composition, age distribution, and detailed demographics are not given. General_public is the broad adult-sample coding, not an assertion of representative sampling. Twelve members were selected for qualitative follow-up interviews and are not an additional independent sample (p. 3, section 3.2; p. 4, section 3.4).
participants.quote: A total of 254 adult participants were initially enrolled, and seven were removed for failing attention checks or offering cursory responses, resulting in a final sample size of 247.
participants.locator: p. 3 (printed p. 10282), sections 3.1-3.2; p. 4, section 3.6; p. 7, section 5 (convenience sample)

ai_tool.how_used: Participants received two or three pre-generated suggestions displayed with the task prompt, in the early or late round according to assignment. Each suggestion was 30-50 words, Flesch-Kincaid reading level 10-12, and pre-rated for creativity M = 5.3 on a 7-point scale. Authors lightly edited GPT-4 outputs after pilot feedback to standardize style and remove inaccuracies. Labeled suggestions had a bold AI-generated heading and a distinctive icon; unlabeled suggestions were attributed to others. No participant chatbot interaction is described (p. 3, section 3.3).

task.description: Propose innovative solutions to reduce urban plastic pollution, feasible within the next five years and meaningful at community level; then refine, expand, combine, or develop new solutions in Round 2. A minimum of 50 words was required after each round. A brick Alternative Uses Task preceded the ideation task as a baseline fluency measure, not an AI-treatment outcome (pp. 3-4, sections 3.3-3.4).
task.duration: Two 5-7-minute ideation rounds in the same session; pre-study assessment 8-10 minutes and post-task evaluation 4-5 minutes. Baseline brick AUT lasted two minutes; the selected follow-up interviews lasted 15-20 minutes (pp. 3-4, section 3.4 and Figure 1).

outcomes.name: Overall creativity of proposed plastic-pollution solutions
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Three domain experts in environmental policy or innovation management independently rated each final idea on novelty, usefulness, and originality using 7-point scales; modified Consensual Assessment Technique; intraclass correlation ≥ 0.80 after calibration (p. 4, section 3.5). Condition-level analyses treat participants as the units; the paper does not report idea-level or rating-level sample counts, or the exact aggregation of expert ratings. The final submission is produced in Round 2. Late-AI groups receive suggestions at the start of that round; Early-AI groups proceed without new external inputs, but removal of their earlier suggestions is not stated (pp. 3-4, section 3.4). Availability is coded mixed to preserve the different exposure schedules and the uncertainty about continued display in Early-AI groups; this is not evidence of a separately tested unassisted after-AI task. The paper reports an overall creativity score but does not specify its formula or how the three dimensions are combined. Final scores and repeated measurements across rounds are retained as one outcome (p. 4, section 4.1; p. 5, section 4.4 and Figure 2a,e). Figure 2 states that shaded regions represent 95% confidence intervals; numerical interval endpoints are not printed (p. 5, caption). Moderator analyses are not treatment-effect coefficients: baseline creativity by condition interaction F(4, 237) = 4.42, p = .002; trust-in-AI moderation p > .17 (p. 5, section 4.3). Table 1 prints baseline-creativity simple slopes (slope, SE, p-value): Control -0.012, 0.031, 0.687; Early-AI-Labeled 0.117, 0.035, 0.005; Early-AI-Unlabeled 0.159, 0.033, < .001; Late-AI-Labeled 0.093, 0.037, 0.029; Late-AI-Unlabeled 0.118, 0.036, 0.005 (p. 5, Table 1). The Alternative Uses Task is a pre-exposure fluency covariate, not a treatment outcome (p. 3, section 3.4).
outcomes.delay: Same experimental session; no delayed assessment (pp. 3-4, section 3.4 and Figure 1).

contrasts.reported: Early-AI-Labeled M = 6.01, SD = 0.48; Control M = 4.94. Post-hoc comparisons are described as favoring both Early-AI groups over Control and Late-AI. The following statistics are the omnibus five-condition test, not this pairwise effect: F(4, 237) = 37.54, p < .001, partial η² = .38. Control SD and pairwise effect, SE, CI, and exact p-value are not printed.

The text states that both Early-AI groups surpassed Control in overall creativity. No numerical Early-AI-Unlabeled mean or SD, or numerical pairwise contrast, is printed in the text or Table 1; group scores are plotted.
The text states that Late-AI groups exceeded Control in final outcomes. No numerical Late-AI-Labeled final mean or SD, or numerical pairwise contrast, is printed; final scores are plotted.
The text states that Late-AI groups exceeded Control in final outcomes. No numerical Late-AI-Unlabeled final mean or SD, or numerical pairwise contrast, is printed; final scores are plotted.

Both Early-AI groups are reported to surpass the Late-AI groups in final overall creativity. This records the stated timing comparison, not a reconstructed pooled-arm estimate; no numerical timing coefficient, SE, or exact pairwise p-value is provided.

Late-AI creativity increases up to +0.88; t = −19.69, p < .001, d = 1.73. The text does not identify whether these statistics refer to a particular Late-AI arm or combine the two arms. These are within-participant changes, not randomized between-arm effects. For context, Early-AI-Labeled changed by +0.17 and Control by +0.14. A repeated-measures ANOVA is described as confirming larger Late-AI improvements, but its F statistic and p-value are not printed.

outcomes.name: Semantic distance from the supplied GPT-4 suggestions (anchoring)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Each participant submission is embedded with text-embedding-ada-002 and compared by cosine similarity with each GPT-4 suggestion; results are reported as semantic distance, with lower distances indicating stronger alignment with the AI suggestions (p. 4, section 3.5). The exact distance transformation and method for aggregating multiple suggestion comparisons are not stated. Condition comparisons are reported for participants, not independent participant-suggestion pairs; the number of scored pairs is not reported. This measures anchoring to supplied AI material, not similarity between different people, so construct is other, question is with_ai, and diversity_detail is left empty. The same measure is reported for final submissions and change across rounds (pp. 4-5, sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.4; Figure 2a,b,e). AI availability differs across rounds and arms; continued display of Early-AI suggestions in Round 2 is not specified (pp. 3-4, section 3.4). One-way/two-way ANOVAs, Tukey HSD where indicated, and mixed-effects models for repeated participant observations are described, but detailed model specifications and standard errors for condition effects are absent (p. 4, section 3.6). The reported correlation with perceived external influence is r = −0.35, p < .001; it is a process association, not an assigned-treatment effect (p. 5, section 4.2 and Figure 2c).
outcomes.delay: Same experimental session; no delayed assessment (pp. 3-4, section 3.4 and Figure 1).

contrasts.reported: Semantic distance: Early-AI-Labeled M = 0.59; Control M = 0.84. The omnibus five-condition test is F(4, 237) = 85.53, p < .001, η² = .59; it is not a pairwise effect. Lower values mean more alignment with AI suggestions. No arm SDs or pairwise SE/CI are printed.

Semantic distance: labeled .61 vs. unlabeled .73; t = −11.04, p < .001, d = 1.58. The positive d is transcribed as printed although labeled distance is lower; no sign-adjusted effect was calculated. The labeling comparison combines timing conditions in the reported description; arm SDs and a numerical CI are not given.

Semantic-distance change ΔM = −0.23, described as the steepest decline across the conditions. The text does not identify a specific Late-AI arm or give a test statistic, SE, SD, or numerical CI for this change; round trajectories are plotted.

assignment.what_was_assigned: Pilot feedback checked the length, clarity, and perceived originality of candidate GPT-4 suggestions. No assignment to AI assistance or comparison conditions is described (p. 3, section 3.3).

participants.exclusions: Not stated. A pilot n = 15 is printed, but the text does not explicitly identify the counted units, participant characteristics, exclusions, or an analyzed-person denominator; people counts are therefore left null.
participants.who: A small pilot provided feedback on the AI stimuli; participant details are not supplied.
participants.quote: Prior to finalizing these AI prompts, we conducted a small pilot study (n = 15) to verify that the suggestions were consistent in length, clarity, and perceived originality.

ai_tool.how_used: AI-generated suggestions were assessed during stimulus preparation, then lightly edited by the authors; no participant creative output under AI assistance is described (p. 3, section 3.3).

task.description: Validate candidate suggestions for length, clarity, and perceived originality. This is a stimulus pretest; no qualifying human-produced creativity or across-person diversity outcome is reported (p. 3, section 3.3).

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: No reuse of another paper’s participants is stated. The interview participants belong to the main experiment; pilot overlap with the main sample is not stated.

company_involvement.description: Coauthor Yishan Huang is affiliated with Beijing Sankuai Network Technology Co., Ltd. The document does not state a separate corporate funding or study-management role.

eligibility.reason: The main study explicitly randomly assigns people to five conditions including a no-AI control (p. 3, sections 3.1-3.3); the stated final analyzed sample is 247 adults, with arm counts 50, 49, 49, 50, and 49 (p. 3, section 3.1); experts score novelty, usefulness, and originality of participant submissions and the results report overall creativity (p. 4, sections 3.5 and 4.1). Late-AI participants explicitly receive GPT-4 suggestions while producing their final Round-2 output (pp. 3-4, section 3.4), so uncertainty over retained access in Early-AI arms does not prevent core eligibility. The pilot does not independently qualify. Semantic distance is to AI suggestions, not across people, so it does not establish an across_people outcome.

one_line_finding: Early-AI-Labeled final creativity was M = 6.01 (SD = 0.48) versus Control M = 4.94, with a five-condition omnibus F(4, 237) = 37.54, p < .001 (p. 4, section 4.1).
open_questions: The final sample is reported as 247, but the one-way omnibus tests repeatedly print F(4, 237); what analysis sample or unreported exclusions account for these degrees of freedom? No replacement sample size is inferred (p. 3, section 3.1; p. 4, sections 3.6 and 4.1).

Were the seven exclusions before or after assignment, and do they include the outliers and incomplete responses mentioned separately? Pre-exclusion randomized counts are not separately recoverable (pp. 3-4, sections 3.1 and 3.6).

Did the Early-AI suggestions remain visible or accessible during Round 2? The procedure says no new external inputs, without stating that earlier suggestions were removed; no definite after_ai outcome is coded (p. 4, section 3.4).

What were the recruitment channel, participant country, and physical setting? The online_rct code follows explicit web delivery, but an online panel or unsupervised remote participation is not explicitly stated (p. 3, sections 3.1 and 3.3; p. 7, section 5).

How were the expert dimension scores combined into overall creativity, and how were distances to multiple AI suggestions aggregated? Outcome-specific person counts, full arm SDs, numerical CIs, and pairwise precision are absent (pp. 4-5, sections 3.5-4.4).
Which Late-AI arm or combination supplies the printed up-to +0.88 change, t = −19.69, d = 1.73, and semantic-distance change ΔM = −0.23? The text does not identify it (p. 5, section 4.4).
For the pilot n = 15, what exactly was counted, and did any pilot participants enter the main experiment? The pilot sample and procedures are only briefly described (p. 3, section 3.3).
notes: Screened on 2026-10-09. Read all PDF pages and all 320 markdown lines, including the references. Locators use PDF page numbers, with printed pagination supplied where useful. Figure/table/appendix inventory: Figure 1 is the procedure; Figure 2a shows final creativity and AI-prompt distance, 2b AI-prompt distance and perceived external influence by labeling, 2c their correlation, 2d baseline-creativity moderation, and 2e changes across rounds; Table 1 gives baseline-creativity slopes. There is no appendix. Five output measures are retained: overall creativity, novelty, usefulness, originality, and AI-prompt semantic distance. Repeated-round versions and moderator analyses remain under those outcomes, not duplicate outcomes. No numerical values were digitized from figures and no effects, participant counts, or SEs were computed. The other measured variables are baseline AUT fluency and trust, perceived external influence, creative self-efficacy, source recognition, and response-time metrics; these are baseline/process/self-report variables, not scored creative-output outcomes (pp. 3-4, sections 3.4-3.5 and Figure 1). For completeness, the printed process statistics are perceived external influence M = 5.36 vs. 4.39, t = 7.22, p < .001, d = 1.03, and 64% source recognition among unlabeled participants (p. 5, section 4.2). The separate pilot is retained as S2 because it is explicitly called a study, although it provides no qualifying participant-output outcome; its n = 15 is not assumed to be an analyzed-people count. Twelve interviews are a subset of S1, not an additional independent experiment. Counts in arms are the final reported sample counts. n_randomized remains null because the document does not separately give counts before screening exclusions. The 254 initially enrolled people are not automatically treated as randomized. No preregistration, data repository, code repository, or supplement link appears in the document. Company involvement is an author affiliation. No other screener form was consulted. Statistics flags identify the types actually available: no complete two-arm mean/SD/n set or pairwise SE is reported. Omnibus eta-squared values and the printed within-person d are retained with their original labels and are not substituted for randomized pairwise effects. No primary outcome is explicitly designated. Across-person diversity is not measured: every reported embedding comparison is against the supplied AI prompts. No separate unassisted post-removal assessment is established.
